tracked_outcomes.title: Manager, Procurement Digitalization
tracked_outcomes.outcome: Pending — hiring manager said "once I wrap up the 1st round, Lacey will be in touch about next steps"
tracked_outcomes.exact_feedback: No formal rejection notice received. Treat as closed for planning purposes.
tracked_outcomes.stage_reached: First-round interview with hiring manager completed
tracked_outcomes.lesson: Procurement knowledge is the explicit gap. Prepare procurement-specific talking points: source-to-pay process, supplier relationship management, contract lifecycle, procurement KPIs (savings, cycle time, supplier performance). unknown.note: Majority of application-only rejections received no feedback. Reduces ability to learn from ATS-level screens.

feedback_quality_note: As of Sep 12, actual interview transcripts have been obtained for both International Motors roles. The hiring manager for the Procurement Digitalization role explicitly stated procurement understanding is "the only gap" in Amber's background. The panel for the Supply Chain Manager role directly questioned Amber's budget ownership experience, noting her $60K budget only covers merit increases and bonuses for 5 direct reports — not capital or operating budgets. Justin Slater (Director, Production IT) asked about managing a "multimillion dollar budget." Both interviews confirmed Amber is still in the first-round pool with decisions expected after interviews conclude "this week and next week." Combined Metals feedback was confirmed by Rachel Hecker. The remaining 22 tracked outcomes have no formal feedback.
